items.name: Soggy Receipt
items.subtitle: A crumpled, water-damaged receipt
items.description: A wadded-up receipt from what appears to be one of Wario's many failed business ventures. The ink has run badly, making most of it illegible. It smells faintly of garlic and engine grease.
items.loreText:
WARIO'S EMPORIUM OF FI--
----------------------------
1x Gold Nose Hair Trim..  3g
1x ???tle of Gar???c Wine  12g
1x 'Legit' Star Piece... 900,000,000,000g
    (CROSSED OUT)
1x Stale Mushroom........ 1g
----------------------------
TOTAL: 16g
PAID: ???
NO REFUNDS. EVER.
HAVE A WARIO DAY!
items.examination: On closer inspection, there's a second receipt stuck to the back. It reads: 'IOU - One favor. Sincerely, W.' The handwriting is barely legible.

obtained.method: Found stuck to the bottom of the crate she arrived in.

stages.label: Crumpled Ball
stages.content: A wet, crumpled ball of paper. Something is printed on it.

stages.label: Partially Unfolded
stages.content: You can make out 'WARIO'S EMPOR--' and a list of prices. The total seems... modest for Wario.

stages.label: Fully Unfolded
stages.content: The full receipt is revealed, including a scratched-out line item for 900 trillion gold. On the back, a handwritten IOU.

items.name: Green T's Battle Plan
items.subtitle: A linen napkin with a frantic battle plan
items.description: A fine linen dinner napkin, clearly stolen from the Corvinarus estate's formal dining set. Green T has scrawled a desperate battle plan across it in what appears to be a mixture of ink and wine. The handwriting grows increasingly erratic toward the edges.
items.loreText:
PLAN:
1. KILL THE VAMPIRES (all of them)
2. SMASH THE CRYSTALS (the big ones)
3. FORCE TIMELINE MERGE
4. UNLEASH THE BEAST (???)
5. RUN

NOTES:
- Stole key from Orangus (DON'T LOSE IT)
- Gun has 3 shots left
- Archie = wildcard (keep him angry)
- If this doesn't work we're all dead anyway
- Tell Remi I'm sorry about the spider thing
items.examination: The napkin has the Corvinarus family crest embroidered in one corner—a dragon coiled around an orange tree. Green T has drawn an arrow pointing to it with the note 'THESE GUYS ARE THE WORST.'

obtained.method: Discovered while snooping around the dining hall after capture by the Onyx Hand.

stages.label: Front (Battle Plan)
stages.content: The frantic battle plan with its five desperate steps.

stages.label: Back (Hidden Message)
stages.content: On the reverse, in much smaller, steadier handwriting: 'If you're reading this and I'm gone—the key opens the FOURTH MIRROR on the second floor. Don't trust the Oracle with the scar. There's only one real one. —GT'

style.customCSS: background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent, transparent 28px, rgba(139,0,0,0.05) 28px, rgba(139,0,0,0.05) 29px);

items.notes: This napkin contains critical tactical intelligence. Green T's plan is reckless but shows deep knowledge of the manor's dimensional mechanics.

items.name: Absurd Rope Replacement Bill
items.subtitle: An outrageously inflated invoice
items.description: A crisp, officially stamped invoice from the Mages' Guild Requisitions Department. It charges Archie Miser for the replacement of one (1) standard hemp rope. The total, after fees, surcharges, taxes, and 'dimensional instability adjustments,' exceeds 2,000 gold pieces.
items.loreText:
═══════════════════════════════
   MAGES' GUILD - INVOICE
   Dept. of Material Requisition
   Form 77-B (Revised)(Revised)
═══════════════════════════════
TO: Archie Miser (Non-Member)
RE: Destruction of Guild Property

Item: Hemp Rope, Standard, 50ft
Base Cost:                    2g
Replacement Fee:             15g
Expedited Processing:        30g
Non-Member Surcharge:        50g
Dimensional Instability Adj: 200g
Planar Hazard Insurance:     300g
Administrative Fee:          150g
Filing Fee:                   75g
Fee Processing Fee:           25g
Ink & Parchment:             12g
Guild Seal Stamping:         40g
Emotional Distress (Staff):  500g
Miscellaneous:               601g
-------------------------------
SUBTOTAL:                 2,000g
Late Fee (pre-applied):      47g
===============================
TOTAL DUE:               2,047g

Payment due IMMEDIATELY.
Failure to pay will result in
collection proceedings and/or
transmutation into a small
rodent.

        [OFFICIAL SEAL]
items.examination: At the very bottom, in tiny print: 'The Mages' Guild is not responsible for transmutation-related injuries, loss of identity, or existential dread. By reading this invoice you agree to our terms of service.'

obtained.method: Handed directly to Archie by a Mages' Guild representative with a completely straight face.

stages.label: Read Calmly
stages.content: You read the invoice. Your eye twitches.

stages.label: Shaking
stages.content: The paper rattles in your grip. 'FEE PROCESSING FEE?!' Two thousand gold for a ROPE?!

items.name: Captured Spy's Field Notes
items.subtitle: Detailed surveillance records
items.description: A small, leather-bound notebook recovered from a captured spy. The handwriting is precise and clinical. It contains detailed observations of Archie Miser and Bones's movements, habits, and conversations. Several pages have been torn out, and others show signs of hasty burning at the edges.
items.loreText:
SUBJECT A (Miser):
- Third eye confirmed. Magical origin unknown.
- Emotional trigger: mentions of fire, past incidents.
- Combat style: reckless. Favors firebolt.
- Weakness: guilt. Exploitable.
- NOTE: Do NOT engage in confined spaces.

SUBJECT B (Bones):
- Former Legion? Unconfirmed.
- Skilled infiltrator. Nearly spotted me twice.
- Has decoded partial cipher set 7.
- Priority: Prevent access to [BURNT]

OPERATIONAL NOTES:
- Dead drop compromised. Switch to [TORN]
- Handler requests extraction by [BURNT]
- If captured: destroy pages 12-15 FIRST
items.examination: Between the pages, you find a tiny folded piece of paper with a crude map. It shows the layout of a building labeled 'PROCESSING FACILITY' with an X marked in what appears to be a sub-basement. The map has been partially burned but the X is still visible.

obtained.method: Recovered from a spy's belongings after capture. The spy attempted to destroy the notebook but was stopped.

stages.label: Surface Reading
stages.content: Standard surveillance notes on Archie and Bones. Professional work.

stages.label: UV Check
stages.content: Holding the pages to light reveals invisible ink between the lines: 'ORACLE IS NOT ONE. ORACLE IS MANY. THE REAL ONE DIED IN 988. WHAT WALKS IS A MEMORY.'

items.notes: The hidden UV message about the Oracle contradicts what the party has been told. If true, it changes everything about the Raventree Manor situation.

items.name: Gray Stone Pendant
items.subtitle: A warm stone pulsing with faint inner light
items.description: A smooth, ovoid gray stone set in a tarnished brass pendant frame. It is slightly warm to the touch and pulses with a faint inner light, like a slow heartbeat. Archaic inscriptions circle the setting—glyphs used in ancient wayfinding magic to mark locations across planes.
items.loreText: The inscriptions, when translated, read: 'I REMEMBER WHERE YOU STOOD.' The stone grows warmer when pointed toward places of significance—battlefields, graves, thresholds between worlds. It is cold and dark when pointed toward nothing.
items.examination: When you hold the pendant up and slowly turn, you notice the inner light brightens noticeably when aimed at the northeast wall. The stone almost thrums against your palm, as if eager to guide you somewhere.

obtained.method: Discovered in an antiquities display case alongside the Cornelius statuette.

stages.label: Front
stages.content: The gray stone pulses gently in its brass frame. The inscriptions glow faintly.

stages.label: Side
stages.content: The brass frame is etched with tiny symbols—each one a different planar coordinate.

stages.label: Back
stages.content: On the reverse of the frame, scratched crudely into the metal: 'PROPERTY OF A.C. — DO NOT REMOVE FROM ESTATE'

items.notes: A.C. likely refers to Aurelian Corvinarus. The pendant may be key to navigating between the fractured planes.

items.name: Star Shard
items.subtitle: A crystalline gift from the Toad God
items.description: A fragment of crystallized divine energy, roughly the size of a closed fist. It radiates a warm, golden light that never dims and hums with a frequency just below the threshold of hearing. The Oracle identified it as a gift from the Toad God—one of the sacred 'Bearer' artifacts that anchor reality itself.
items.loreText: When held, the Star Shard imparts a feeling of profound peace and absolute certainty. You know, with a conviction that transcends logic, that this object is IMPORTANT. Not important in the way gold or weapons are important—important in the way gravity is important. It is a fundamental piece of something vast.
items.examination: Looking deep into the crystal's core, you see what appears to be a tiny star—a pinprick of light that shifts through colors no mortal palette contains. Staring too long makes your eyes water and fills your mind with a sound like distant singing.

obtained.method: Revealed by one of the multiple Oracles during the pre-ritual gathering. Declared to be a 'Bearer' artifact.

stages.label: Surface Glow
stages.content: The shard glows with steady golden light. It feels warm and alive in your hands.

stages.label: Deep Resonance
stages.content: As you focus, you hear fragments of a celestial hymn. Words form in your mind: 'THE BEARER WALKS BETWEEN. THE SHARD REMEMBERS ALL PATHS. THREE WERE MADE. TWO REMAIN. ONE IS LOST IN THE DEEP MIRROR.'

items.notes: One of three Star Shards. Two remain; one is lost in the Deep Mirror. This may be the key to the planar convergence.

items.name: Cracked Brass Compass
items.subtitle: A divination compass with a shattered face
items.description: A palm-sized brass compass with a cracked glass face. The needle doesn't point north—it points toward sources of magical energy, spinning lazily between them. The casing is dented and scratched, suggesting it has survived considerable abuse. Faint divination magic radiates from it in irregular pulses.
items.loreText: The compass was provided by Agent L (Luigi) as part of the Mages' Guild cleanup contract. It detects magical signatures within approximately 100 feet, with the needle spinning faster as the source grows nearer. The crack in the glass occurred during a dimensional transit, and the compass has been slightly 'off' ever since—occasionally pointing at things that aren't there yet.
items.examination: The compass back is engraved with a serial number: 'MG-DIV-0047.' Below it, someone has scratched: 'It shows you where magic IS, not where it SHOULD BE. Be careful. —L'

obtained.method: Provided by Agent L (Luigi) as part of the ghost-hunting contract equipment.

stages.label: Resting
stages.content: The needle drifts lazily, pointing vaguely east. The glass crack runs diagonally across the face.

stages.label: Active
stages.content: The needle suddenly spins rapidly, then locks onto a direction behind you. The brass casing grows warm.

stages.label: Anomaly
stages.content: The needle points straight DOWN. Through the cracked glass, you glimpse something that isn't reflected in the room—a doorway that doesn't exist. Yet.

items.notes: Stolen by Purple T when he picked Archie's pockets and used to open a portal. Currently missing.

items.name: Iron Legion Insignia
items.subtitle: A branded military identification badge
items.description: A small iron badge in the shape of a clenched fist, stamped with the Iron Legion's motto: 'STRENGTH THROUGH ORDER.' This particular insignia was surgically implanted beneath the skin of a toad the party rescued, revealing him as a Legion plant. The badge still has traces of dried blood and surgical adhesive on its back.
items.loreText: Iron Legion insignias come in three tiers: bronze (recruit), iron (operative), and blacksteel (commander). This one is iron-tier, indicating the plant was a trained operative—not a simple informant. The serial number on the back (IL-7-4412) corresponds to the 7th Division, 44th Infiltration Unit, Agent 12.
items.examination: Under magnification, the fist emblem has micro-engraved text spiraling inward: 'THE LEGION ENDURES. THE INDIVIDUAL SERVES. FAILURE IS TREASON. TREASON IS DEATH.' Cheery.

obtained.method: Discovered during emergency surgery on a 'rescued' toad. The insignia was implanted subcutaneously in the toad's shoulder.

stages.label: Front (Emblem)
stages.content: The Iron Fist emblem, cold and heavy. 'STRENGTH THROUGH ORDER' stamped around the border.

stages.label: Back (Serial)
stages.content: Serial: IL-7-4412. Below it, a QR-like pattern of dots that may encode additional information. There are faint stains that could be blood—or rust.

items.notes: This badge proves the Iron Legion had agents embedded among the trafficked toads. The entire rescue may have been orchestrated.

items.name: Entropy Ring
items.subtitle: A coercive magical restraint device
items.description: A plain black iron ring that seems to absorb light. When worn, it creates a magical bond between the wearer and the ring's controller, allowing remote tracking, communication, and—if activated—excruciating pain. The ring cannot be removed without the controller's command or specialized dispel magic. Agent Malissia fitted one to Toadburt during his captivity.
items.loreText: The ring is warm to the touch despite its black surface. It vibrates faintly at irregular intervals—receiving signals from its controller. The interior surface is inscribed with binding runes that glow a dull red when the wearer attempts to resist commands. Each pulse of vibration is accompanied by a whispered word in a language that shouldn't exist.
items.examination: Examining the ring with detect magic reveals THREE distinct enchantments layered on top of each other: Tracking (Divination), Communication (Enchantment), and Pain Compliance (Necromancy). The necromantic layer is the strongest. Whoever made this ring was skilled and cruel.

obtained.method: Fitted to Toadburt by Agent Malissia of the Iron Legion during magical interrogation.

stages.label: Surface
stages.content: A black ring. It feels wrong. Your skin crawls when you touch it.

stages.label: Rune Translation
stages.content: The binding runes translate roughly to: 'OBEY OR SUFFER. SERVE OR BURN. THREE DAYS. BRING THE ORACLE. OR THE RING REMEMBERS.' The three-day deadline has passed. What happens now?

items.notes: The ring's three-day deadline has expired. Toadburt's status is unknown. The ring may have a failsafe.

items.name: Honorary Fellowship Badge
items.subtitle: A suspiciously fast-tracked Guild credential
items.description: A polished bronze badge bearing the Mages' Guild crest—an open book beneath a constellation. It identifies the bearer as an Honorary Fellow of the Guild, granting limited access to Guild facilities and resources. Archie received this as part of his ghost-hunting contract, but he detected faint, unfamiliar magic emanating from it that isn't part of standard Guild enchantment.
items.loreText: The badge reads: 'HONORARY FELLOW — ARCHIE MISER — By authority of the Raventree Chapter — Provisional Status — NOT FOR RESALE.' The 'Provisional Status' text is in much smaller font than everything else.
items.examination: Using detect magic on the badge reveals the expected identification enchantment, but also a secondary, hidden aura—something between Divination and Enchantment. It's subtle, almost imperceptible. Is the Guild tracking him? Influencing him? Or is it just standard security? The fact that they fast-tracked this for a known fire hazard is suspicious enough.

obtained.method: Issued by the Mages' Guild as part of the ghost-hunting contract negotiations. Archie accepted it despite his suspicions.

stages.label: Front (Official)
stages.content: The Guild crest gleams. 'HONORARY FELLOW — ARCHIE MISER.' It looks legitimate.

stages.label: Back (Suspicious)
stages.content: The back has a Guild registration number and a tiny rune that Archie doesn't recognize. When he touched it, it pulsed once—warm, brief, like a heartbeat. Then nothing.

items.notes: Dan's inventory notes mention a similar tracking badge that 'burns if removed improperly.' Are all Guild badges like this?

items.name: Markop's Father's Photograph
items.subtitle: A faded, creased photograph
items.description: A small, creased photograph showing a middle-aged man in working clothes standing in front of what appears to be a blacksmith's forge. His face is weathered but kind, and he's holding a hammer in one hand and a small child's hand in the other. The child's face is turned away from the camera. The photograph is water-stained and has been folded and unfolded many times.
items.loreText: On the back, in faded pencil: 'Papa and me. Summer, before he left.' Nothing else. No date, no location, no explanation of where he went or why.
items.examination: In the background of the photograph, partially obscured by smoke from the forge, there's a sign you can barely make out. It reads: '—KROP'S IRON—' The forge has a distinctive anvil with a crack running through it. If this forge still exists somewhere, it could be a lead.

obtained.method: Discovered among personal effects scattered in the dilapidated east wing during the manor exploration.

stages.label: Front (Photo)
stages.content: A man and a child at a forge. The image is faded but the man's expression is unmistakable—pride, love, and something else. Worry, maybe. Like he knows he's running out of time.

stages.label: Back (Inscription)
stages.content: 'Papa and me. Summer, before he left.' The pencil is so faded you have to tilt the photo to catch the light. Below the words, a small drawn star—a child's addition.

items.notes: The forge sign ('—KROP'S IRON—') could match 'Markop's Iron Works.' The cracked anvil is a distinctive identifier.

items.name: Dragonus Cornelius Statuette
items.subtitle: An ancient stone figure of a dragon-robed noble
items.description: A small statuette carved from dark gray stone, roughly eight inches tall. It depicts a regal figure wearing elaborate dragon-scale robes and holding a sphere in one hand and a curved blade in the other. The face is obscured by a hood, but the eyes are inlaid with tiny chips of orange amber that seem to catch light from impossible angles.
items.loreText: The base is inscribed: 'DRAGONUS CORNELIUS — FIRST OF THE LINE — BINDER OF THE FLAME — 901 BF.' The Corvinarus family traces their power to this figure, who allegedly bound a dragon's essence to his bloodline through a forbidden ritual. The statuette predates the current manor by over a century.
items.examination: The sphere in the figure's hand has a tiny crack, and when you press your ear to it, you can hear something—not sound exactly, but a vibration. Like a heartbeat. Or an egg about to hatch. The curved blade appears to be stained at the tip, even in stone. The sculptor captured a single drop of blood falling from its edge.

obtained.method: Uncovered in a display case alongside the Gray Stone Pendant and a shattered mirror.

stages.label: Overview
stages.content: A stone figure of austere power. The orange amber eyes catch your gaze and hold it.

stages.label: Base Inscription
stages.content: 'DRAGONUS CORNELIUS — FIRST OF THE LINE — BINDER OF THE FLAME — 901 BF.' Below, in smaller text: 'Let the blood remember what the mind forgets.'

stages.label: Hidden Detail
stages.content: The drop of blood on the carved blade isn't stone. It's real—preserved, crystalized, still faintly warm after 139 years. This statuette contains actual blood of the Cornelius bloodline.

items.notes: Hjumpik's vision at Highsun 26 showed an orange-robed figure cutting their palm over a dragon egg in 988 BF. This statuette dates from 901 BF—87 years earlier. The Cornelius bloodline's pact with dragons may be even older than believed.

items.name: Fawful Propaganda Leaflet
items.subtitle: A garish, crumpled recruitment flyer
items.description: A cheaply printed leaflet on bright green paper, featuring Fawful's distinctive grinning face above a wall of barely coherent text. These have been dropping from airships and posted on walls across the Mushroom Kingdom. The grammar is atrocious but the message is clear: submit or suffer.
items.loreText:
🟢 FAWFUL IS HAVING THE FURY OF GREATNESS! 🟢

Citizens of the Mushrooming Kingdom!

Your princess is being DEAD for many years!
Your chancellor is being USELESS for more years!
Your kingdom is being PATHETIC for ALL the years!

BUT FAWFUL! Fawful is having the PLAN!
Fawful is having the POWER!
Fawful is having the CASTLE!
(It is being Fawful's castle now. Do not be visiting
without the appointment.)

JOIN FAWFUL and be having:
✓ Regular meals (probably)
✓ Protection from dragons (Fawful has MANY dragons)
✓ The satisfaction of WINNING

DO NOT JOIN FAWFUL and be having:
✗ Regret
✗ Also explosions

FAWFUL HAS FURY!

[Printed by Fawful Press™ — All rights reserved
by Fawful because Fawful is reserving ALL things]
items.examination: On the back, someone has drawn a crude caricature of Fawful with crossed-out eyes and the word 'NEVER' written in bold. Below it, in different handwriting: 'The Loyalists were right. We should have listened.' This leaflet has been passed between resistance sympathizers.

obtained.method: Found plastered to the wall of the restaurant where the Iron Legion raid occurred.

stages.label: Front (Propaganda)
stages.content: Fawful's grinning face stares at you from bright green paper. The text is a masterclass in megalomaniacal grammar.

stages.label: Back (Resistance)
stages.content: A crude drawing of Fawful, crossed out. 'NEVER' in bold. Below: 'The Loyalists were right. We should have listened.' Two sets of handwriting. Two people who've had enough.

style.customCSS: border: 3px solid #00CC00; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, #e8ffe8, #c8f0c8); color: #1a3a1a;

items.notes: Fawful's propaganda is laughably bad, but his military results speak for themselves. He holds Peach's Castle.

items.name: Corvinarus Vampire Wine
items.subtitle: An ancient bottle of questionable vintage
items.description: A tall, slender bottle of deep burgundy glass, sealed with black wax bearing the Corvinarus dragon crest. The wine inside is almost black—too dark to be any normal grape. It sloshes with an unsettling thickness, and when held up to light, something moves inside that isn't liquid. Wario acquired this from unknown sources and traded it to Hjumpik.
items.loreText:
The label, written in elegant calligraphy on aged vellum, reads:

'CHÂTEAU CORVINARUS
Vintage: 955 BF
Varietal: Sanguis Noctis
Estate Bottled

Tasting Notes: Bold, with undertones of iron,
despair, and something older than memory.
Pairs well with betrayal.

WARNING: Not for mortal consumption.
Side effects may include: heightened senses,
photosensitivity, existential dread, and an
irresistible urge to count things.

Serve at room temperature (of a crypt).'
items.examination: The year 955 BF is the same year Princess Peach was assassinated. Coincidence? The bottle has never been opened—the wax seal is intact. But something inside the bottle is definitely aware of you. When you look away and look back, the liquid level has changed.

obtained.method: Acquired from Wario's inventory during a trade negotiation in the fairy village.

stages.label: Still
stages.content: The dark liquid sits motionless. The bottle is cold despite the warm room.

stages.label: Swirled
stages.content: The wine moves wrong—too slow, too thick. As it settles, you swear you see a face form in the liquid for just a moment. It's smiling.

style.customCSS: background: radial-gradient(ellipse at center, #1a0008 0%, #0a0004 100%); border: 1px solid #4a0020;

items.notes: DO NOT DRINK. Vintage 955 BF—the year of the assassination. The Corvinarus family was bottling something that year. What were they celebrating? Or mourning?

items.name: Removed Guild Tracking Badge
items.subtitle: A forcibly extracted surveillance device
items.description: A small, circular badge similar to Archie's Fellowship Badge, but this one has been violently torn from its owner. The edges are bent and there are scorch marks where the removal triggered its anti-tampering enchantment. Purple T ripped these from Dan and the other mages before their unauthorized departure through a Guild portal.
items.loreText: The badge's surface is cracked, but the tracking rune on the back still pulses weakly—a dying heartbeat. Every few seconds, it emits a faint blue glow as it tries to transmit a location that no longer makes sense. The enchantment is breaking down, but it hasn't stopped trying.
items.examination: The anti-tamper burn pattern is distinctive: three concentric circles radiating from the center, each representing a layer of enchantment. The outermost (tracking) is shattered. The middle (identification) is fading. The innermost... is still active. It's not tracking location. It's recording everything said within five feet of it.

obtained.method: Violently removed from Dan and other mages by Purple T to avoid Guild detection before unauthorized portal transit.

stages.label: Outer Layer (Broken)
stages.content: Tracking enchantment: DESTROYED. No longer transmitting location data.

stages.label: Middle Layer (Fading)
stages.content: Identification enchantment: DEGRADED. The badge still identifies Dan as 'DAN-FIELD-OPS-7' but the signal is corrupted.

stages.label: Inner Layer (ACTIVE)
stages.content: ⚠️ AUDIO RECORDING ENCHANTMENT: STILL ACTIVE. This badge has been recording all nearby conversations since it was issued. The Guild has been listening to EVERYTHING.

style.customCSS: border: 2px dashed #CC0000; animation: warningPulse 2s ease-in-out infinite;

items.notes: If the inner recording layer is still active, the Guild may have a complete audio log of Dan's conversations—including discussions of plans, allies, and secrets. This changes the threat assessment of the Mages' Guild significantly.

items.name: X.O.'s Staff Fragment
items.subtitle: A piece of the staff that powered the Vigilance
items.description: A six-inch fragment of the crystalline staff once wielded by the traitor X.O. The full staff was used to restore power to the Vigilance's core after hjumpik disabled it with an axe. This fragment broke off during the power restoration and still crackles with residual energy—miniature lightning arcs between the crystal facets at irregular intervals.
items.loreText: The crystal is unlike any natural mineral. It's translucent with a deep violet core that shifts to electric blue at the edges. When gripped, it vibrates at a frequency that makes your teeth ache and fills your vision with afterimages of places you've never been. The energy it contains is immense—this single fragment could power a small building for a month.
items.examination: Deep within the crystal's core, suspended in the violet light, there appears to be a tiny, perfectly preserved feather. It's too small to identify the species, but it glows with its own inner light—a warm gold that contrasts sharply with the staff's cold energy. Was X.O.'s power not entirely her own?

obtained.method: Broke off from X.O.'s staff during the emergency power restoration. hjumpik kept the fragment.

stages.label: Dormant
stages.content: The crystal hums quietly. Tiny arcs of electricity dance between its facets.

stages.label: Activated
stages.content: The fragment flares with violet light! For a brief instant, you see a vision: X.O. standing before a massive tree made entirely of lightning, receiving the staff from a figure made of feathers and starlight. Then the vision fades, and the fragment goes dark. It needs time to recharge.

items.notes: X.O.'s full staff powered an entire airship. This fragment still contains enormous energy. The feather inside suggests X.O. received her power from a celestial entity. Related to the Star Shards?

items.name: Crumpled Receipt
items.shortDescription: A wadded-up receipt from a tavern. Smells like old beer.
items.fullDescription: A crumpled, beer-stained receipt from 'The Soggy Biscuit Tavern'. Most of the ink has run, but you can make out: '3x Ale, 1x Mystery Meat Pie, 1x "The Regret" (house special)'. Someone has written 'NEVER AGAIN' in shaky handwriting on the back.
items.hiddenContent: On the back, barely visible: 'Tell Manny the password is TURNIP. Third booth. Don't order the pie.' — This was likely a dead drop note repurposed as scratch paper.

interactionStyle.footerText: The ink is fading. This won't last much longer.
interactionStyle.customRevealCSS: @keyframes paperUnfold { 0% { transform: scaleY(0.1) rotate(3deg); opacity: 0.3; filter: blur(2px); } 50% { transform: scaleY(0.8) rotate(-1deg); opacity: 0.8; filter: blur(0.5px); } 100% { transform: scaleY(1) rotate(0); opacity: 1; filter: blur(0); } }

onHover.css: transform: translateX(1px) rotate(-2deg); transition: transform 0.2s ease;

items.name: Battle Plan Napkin
items.shortDescription: A linen napkin with Green T's frantic battle plan scrawled in what appears to be cranberry sauce.
items.fullDescription: A fine linen dinner napkin, now ruined by frantic scrawling in dark red sauce. Green T's unmistakable block lettering details an assault plan: arrows pointing to 'CRYSTAL POINTS', X marks over 'VAMPIRE LORDS', and a crude drawing of what might be a beast breaking free from chains. The napkin is still slightly damp.
items.hiddenContent: The reverse side has a hastily drawn map of the manor's lower levels. Three locations are circled and labeled: 'ANCHOR 1 — Ballroom', 'ANCHOR 2 — Cellar', 'ANCHOR 3 — Tower'. A note reads: 'Break ALL THREE or it means nothing. The Beast will handle the rest. — GT'

interactionStyle.footerText: The sauce is still wet. Written within the last hour.

items.name: Gray Stone Pendant
items.shortDescription: A smooth, warm gray stone in a brass pendant frame. It pulses with faint inner light.
items.fullDescription: A perfectly smooth gray stone, slightly warm to the touch, set within a tarnished brass pendant frame. Faint light pulses from deep within the stone at irregular intervals, like a slow heartbeat. Archaic inscriptions ring the brass frame — location-marking runes used by pre-war cartographers. The chain is missing.
items.hiddenContent: The runes, when translated, read: 'WHERE THE BEARER STANDS, THE STONE REMEMBERS.' This is a waypoint marker — it records geographic locations when activated. Currently, it holds three saved locations, visible as tiny pinpricks of light within the stone.

items.name: Iron Legion Insignia
items.shortDescription: A small iron pin found surgically embedded beneath a toad's skin. Proof of infiltration.
items.fullDescription: A tiny iron pin in the shape of a gauntleted fist, discovered during emergency surgery on a rescued toad. The pin was surgically implanted beneath the skin of the forearm, invisible to the naked eye. It bears micro-engravings: a serial number and the words 'LOYAL UNTO IRON'.
items.interactionPrompt: Hold the pin up to the light...
items.hiddenContent: Under magnification, the serial number reads 'IL-7749-REDTHORN'. Cross-referencing with captured Legion documents reveals this designation belongs to Unit 'Redthorn' — a deep-cover infiltration squad specializing in toad communities. The pin also functions as a low-range magical transponder.

interactionStyle.footerText: ⚠ TRANSPONDER STILL ACTIVE — Handle with care

items.name: X.O.'s Staff (Power Core)
items.shortDescription: The staff that X.O. used to seize the Vigilance. Now repurposed as the ship's emergency power source.
items.fullDescription: A sleek, obsidian-black staff approximately four feet in length, crowned with a crystalline matrix that hums with contained energy. Originally wielded by X.O. during her betrayal, the staff was confiscated after her defeat and jury-rigged into the Vigilance's power core. The crystal pulses with a deep violet light.
items.interactionPrompt: Place your hand on the crystal...
items.hiddenContent: The crystal responds to touch with a flash of imagery: a floating fortress above clouds, rows of identical soldiers, and a woman's voice saying 'Phase Two is inevitable.' The staff contains residual memories of X.O.'s plans — plans that extend far beyond the Vigilance.

interactionStyle.footerText: The crystal grows warm. Something stirs within.

items.name: Mirror Warning Note
items.shortDescription: A hastily written note warning: 'DO NOT CLEAN THE MIRRORS.'
items.fullDescription: A small, yellowed piece of parchment found tucked behind a crumbling baseboard in the east wing. The handwriting is shaky but deliberate. The ink is old but the paper is surprisingly well-preserved, as if the warning itself resists decay.
items.hiddenContent:
The full note reads: 'DO NOT CLEAN THE MIRRORS. They are not reflections. They are DOORS. If the glass is clear, THEY can see you. If THEY see you, THEY reach. The dust is the only thing keeping them blind. — F.C., Year 1012'

F.C. — likely a former resident or servant. This predates the party's arrival by nearly 30 years.

interactionStyle.footerText: The paper crumbles slightly at the edges as you handle it.
interactionStyle.customRevealCSS: @keyframes unfoldGentle { 0% { transform: scaleY(0.1) rotate(2deg); opacity:0.3; } 100% { transform: scaleY(1) rotate(0); opacity:1; } }

items.name: Entropy Ring
items.shortDescription: A black iron ring that burns with cold. Fitted to Toadburt by Agent Malissia as a control device.
items.fullDescription: A ring of black iron so dark it seems to absorb light. The inner surface is inscribed with entropy-class sigils that glow a sickly green when the ring is active. It serves as both a tracking device and a kill-switch.
items.interactionPrompt: Study the sigils on the inner band...
items.hiddenContent: The sigils translate to a binding contract: 'THE BEARER SERVES. THE BEARER REPORTS. THE BEARER EXPIRES AT THE HOLDER'S WILL. Duration: 336 hours from activation. Handler: MALISSIA, AGENT CLASS VII.' A countdown is etched into the band in magical script, though it has since expired. The ring is now inert — but still cannot be removed.

interactionStyle.footerText: STATUS: EXPIRED — Ring remains bonded to host tissue.

items.name: Faded Photograph
items.shortDescription: A water-damaged photograph of a man who looks remarkably like Markop. His father?
items.fullDescription: A small, dog-eared photograph with severe water damage along the bottom edge. The image shows a broad-shouldered man standing in front of what appears to be a smithy. The resemblance to Markop is unmistakable. The back is blank except for a faded date: '1018 BF'.
items.hiddenContent: Under the date, barely visible in pencil: 'Last day at the forge. They came for me at dawn. Tell M— I tried.' The writing trails off as if interrupted. The pencil lead broke mid-sentence.

interactionStyle.footerText: The pencil lead broke here. He didn't finish.

items.name: Cracked Brass Compass
items.shortDescription: A brass compass radiating faint divination magic. Its needle doesn't point north — it points to portals.
items.fullDescription: A pocket-sized brass compass with a cracked glass face. The needle is made of an unknown silvery metal that vibrates when near planar boundaries. Agent L provided it to Archie. Later stolen by Purple Toad, who used it to open a portal and escape.
items.hiddenContent: The compass has a secondary function: when the glass is pressed three times in rapid succession, it emits a high-pitched tone inaudible to most species but painful to fey creatures. The back panel is engraved: 'PROPERTY OF E. GADD LABORATORIES — PROTOTYPE 7.' It was never meant to leave the lab.

interactionStyle.footerText: E. GADD LABORATORIES — Not for field deployment.

items.name: Absurd Rope Bill
items.shortDescription: A bloated invoice from the Mages' Guild for a broken rope. Total: over 2,000 gold.
items.fullDescription: An official Mages' Guild invoice on pristine enchanted parchment. Line items include: 'Rope (Standard, 50ft) — 2gp', 'Emergency Requisition Fee — 150gp', 'Interdimensional Filing Fee — 500gp', 'Senior Mage Consultation Fee — 400gp', 'Convenience Fee — 250gp'. Total: 2,016gp.
items.hiddenContent: In microscopic text at the bottom: 'Failure to pay within 30 days will result in the addition of a Late Payment Curse (Form 12-C), which causes mild but persistent itching in the dominant hand. Appeals may be filed in triplicate to the Office of Fiscal Sorcery, between the hours of 3:00 AM and 3:15 AM on alternating Wednesdays.'

interactionStyle.footerText: Payment due: IMMEDIATELY. The Guild seal glows red.

onHover.css: transform: rotate(-1deg) scale(0.98); cursor: grabbing; transition: all 0.2s ease;

items.name: Star Shard
items.shortDescription: A crystalline gift from the Toad God. It hums with divine resonance.
items.fullDescription: A fragment of pure crystallized starlight, roughly the size of a fist, that emits a warm, golden glow. The Oracle revealed it as a gift from the Toad God — a 'Bearer's Shard' that serves as both a key and a conduit for divine energy. Tiny motes of light drift through its interior like distant galaxies.
items.interactionPrompt: Focus your will into the shard...
items.hiddenContent: The shard responds to sincere intention. When truly needed, it can: 1) Illuminate a path through any darkness, 2) Reveal hidden truths by burning away illusions, 3) Serve as an anchor point during planar travel. However, each use diminishes the shard slightly. The Oracle warned it has 'perhaps three uses remaining before it returns to the sky.'

interactionStyle.footerText: Three uses remain. The light dims with each invocation.

items.name: Purple Toad's Fortune Song
items.shortDescription: A transcription of the cryptic fortune-telling song sung by Purple Toad before he vanished through a portal.
items.fullDescription: Archie transcribed this from memory after regaining consciousness. The Purple Toad entered, sang this strange song while systematically pickpocketing Archie, asked about planar portals, used Archie's own stolen compass to open one, and stepped through.
items.hiddenContent:
♪ Shuffle the deck, dear hero mine,
The cards are cut, the stars align.
A fool walks forward, blind and bright,
Into a door that eats the light.

Three eyes see what two cannot,
The third reveals the tangled knot.
But he who pulls the thread too fast
Will find the future eats the past.

The orange tree bears bitter fruit,
The serpent coils around the root.
The mirror cracks from side to side,
The curse has found a place to hide.

So shuffle the deck, dear hero mine,
Your card is drawn — ♪

(The song cuts off here. Purple Toad had already stepped through the portal.)

interactionStyle.footerText: He was already gone before the last note faded.

items.name: Mini-Mushroom
items.shortDescription: A tiny blue mushroom that shrinks the consumer. Required to access the barrel compartments hiding trafficked toads.
items.fullDescription: A mushroom roughly the size of a thimble, with a bright blue cap covered in white spots. When consumed, the user shrinks to approximately 1/10th their normal size for about one hour. Over 150 toads are hidden in barrel compartments accessible only at miniature size.
items.hiddenContent: The mushroom smells like fresh rain and cedar wood. A faint marking on the stem, visible only under magnification, reads 'BM-CROP-7' — suggesting these are cultivated, not wild. Someone is farming Mini-Mushrooms specifically for the trafficking operation. The growing conditions required (perpetual twilight, volcanic soil) narrow the source to only three known locations.

interactionStyle.footerText: Source narrowed to three locations. Investigation pending.

items.name: War Mage's Staff
items.shortDescription: A staff recovered from the Matriarch's hoard, claimed by Markop for Archie's use.
items.fullDescription: A staff of dark ironwood, roughly five feet long, capped with a head of raw, uncut garnet that pulses with contained destructive energy. The wood is carved with angular runes associated with evocation magic — specifically fire and force.
items.hiddenContent: The staff resonates strongly with fire magic, amplifying flame-based spells by an estimated 20%. However, the garnet head has a flaw — a tiny crack that occasionally causes spells to 'leak.' The handprint scorch mark on the wood is a maker's mark. Inside the repaired crack, there's a sliver of dragonscale — connecting this weapon to the Corvinarus dragon-grafting tradition.

interactionStyle.footerText: The garnet grows warm. It remembers fire.

items.name: Orangus's Stolen Key
items.shortDescription: A key stolen from Orangus Cornelius during the Shadow Estate dinner. Opens an unknown lock.
items.fullDescription: An ornate key of dark metal, roughly four inches long, with a handle shaped like a coiled serpent. Green T pickpocketed this from Orangus Cornelius. The serpent's eyes are set with tiny red stones that glow faintly in darkness.
items.interactionPrompt: Hold the key up to the darkness...
items.hiddenContent: In complete darkness, the red stones project a faint pattern onto nearby surfaces — a map fragment showing a room beneath the manor's cellar that doesn't appear on any known floor plan. The serpent's mouth, when pressed, reveals a hidden compartment in the handle containing a coiled piece of wire — either a lockpick or a secondary key.

interactionStyle.footerText: The serpent watches. Even now.

items.name: Poltergust 3000 (Full Tank)
items.shortDescription: Luigi's ghost-catching vacuum. Currently at maximum capacity with captured entities.
items.fullDescription: A modified backpack-mounted vacuum device designed by Professor E. Gadd. The tank currently glows with compressed energy of multiple captured ghosts. A pressure gauge reads 'FULL — DO NOT ADD MORE'.
items.hiddenContent: Through the reinforced glass, you can see the compressed ghosts swirling in a miniature vortex. One appears to be mouthing words — lip-reading suggests it's repeating 'THE MIRRORS WERE FIRST' over and over. The tank's serial plate reads 'POLTERGUST 3000 — Unit #7 — FIELD PROTOTYPE — Property of E. Gadd Labs — IF FOUND, DO NOT OPEN. SERIOUSLY. DON'T.'

interactionStyle.footerText: ⚠ UNIT #7 — E. GADD LABS — DO NOT OPEN

items.name: Captured Spy's Field Notes
items.shortDescription: Detailed surveillance notes left behind by a captured spy. Documents Archie and Bones' activities.
items.fullDescription: A leather-bound field notebook containing meticulous surveillance records written in coded shorthand. The notes document weeks of observation of Archie and Bones. The level of detail is unsettling — the spy knew what Archie ate for breakfast.
items.hiddenContent:
The decoded notes reveal: 'Subject A (Archie) — Third Eye is the priority. Extraction method undetermined. Guild wants it intact. Legion wants it destroyed. Onyx Hand wants to EAT it. Recommendation: maintain distance. Subject A is unpredictable and willing to use maximum force with minimum provocation.'

ADDENDUM: 'Subject A showed mercy to [REDACTED] on Highsun 15. This is exploitable.'

Final entry: 'COVER BLOWN. Burn protocols initiated. If you're reading this, I'm already extracted. Good luck.'

interactionStyle.footerText: BURN PROTOCOL COMPLETE — Source extracted.

onHover.css: border-color: #ff4400; box-shadow: inset 0 0 30px rgba(255,68,0,0.1); transition: all 0.2s ease;

items.name: Wario's Infinite Catalogue
items.shortDescription: A 2,361-item wish-list/price catalogue. The Star Rod is listed at 900 trillion coins.
items.fullDescription: An impossibly long scroll that unfurls to roughly forty feet in length, covered in Wario's barely legible handwriting. It lists 2,361 items with increasingly absurd prices. The scroll smells strongly of garlic and gold polish.
items.hiddenContent:
Hidden among the absurd listings are three legitimate entries that appear to be coded messages:
#847: One (1) Soul Jar — PRICE: Information about the Bearer
#1203: Null Key — PRICE: The location of the Original
#2360: Exit Token — PRICE: A name the Toad God has forgotten.

These suggest Wario is far more connected to the metaphysical conflict than he lets on.

interactionStyle.footerText: Wario knows more than he's selling.

onHover.css: box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(255,204,0,0.5); border-color: #ffee44; transition: all 0.3s ease;

items.name: Divination Incense Candles
items.shortDescription: Rare incense that forces a constitution save. Failure means unconsciousness.
items.fullDescription: Three slender candles of deep violet wax, each roughly six inches long. They smell faintly of lavender and burnt copper. Purple T stole these specifically to use against Archie.
items.hiddenContent: The candles are labeled: 'RESTRICTED — CLASS IV DIVINATION AID. Not for field use. Side effects include: vivid prophetic dreams, temporary loss of motor function, speaking in tongues, mild to severe existential dread. Do not use more than one candle per 24-hour period. Do not use near open flames (ironic, we know).' — Guild Alchemy Dept.

interactionStyle.footerText: Three candles remain. Use with extreme caution.

onHover.css: filter: brightness(1.1) contrast(1.1); box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(136,68,170,0.4); transition: all 0.3s ease;

items.name: Mages' Guild Tracking Badge
items.shortDescription: A small metallic badge that burns if removed improperly. Part of the Guild's surveillance apparatus.
items.fullDescription: A coin-sized badge bearing the Mages' Guild emblem — an open book wreathed in flame. It bonds magically to the wearer's skin after 24 hours. If removed without the proper counter-sigil, it burns the wearer and sends an alert. Dan described it as 'part leash, part insurance policy.'
items.interactionPrompt: Inspect the back of the badge...
items.hiddenContent: The back contains a micro-engraved serial number and a tracking sigil broadcasting the wearer's location every 30 seconds. Dan's notes reveal the badge also records ambient sound within a 10-foot radius, making every badge-wearer an unwitting surveillance device for the Guild.

interactionStyle.footerText: ⚠ Badge also functions as audio surveillance device.

items.name: Blackite Wand (Guild Leash)
items.shortDescription: A wand made of blackite crystal. Dan describes it as functioning like 'a leash.'
items.fullDescription: A wand approximately eight inches long, carved from a single piece of blackite — a rare crystal that absorbs magical energy. Dan's notes reveal its true purpose: it suppresses the user's innate magical abilities while broadcasting their magical signature to Guild monitors.
items.hiddenContent: When magic is channeled through the wand, approximately 30% of the energy is siphoned off and stored in the blackite crystal. Dan's notes theorize this stored energy is periodically harvested by Guild Archivists. The wand also records every spell cast through it — type, power level, target, and location. Handle inscription: 'GUILD ISSUE — DO NOT MODIFY — PENALTY: EXPULSION.'

interactionStyle.footerText: 30% energy drain confirmed. Every spell logged.

onHover.css: filter: brightness(0.85); border-color: #6644aa; transition: all 0.3s ease;

items.name: Dragonus Cornelius Statuette
items.shortDescription: A small figurine depicting a dragon-humanoid hybrid in ornate robes. The Corvinarus family crest is carved into the base.
items.fullDescription: A meticulously carved statuette, roughly six inches tall, depicting a figure that is half-dragon, half-humanoid wearing flowing robes. The base bears the Corvinarus family crest — an ouroboros serpent encircling a crescent moon. The material appears to be dragonbone.
items.interactionPrompt: Turn the statuette in your hands...
items.hiddenContent: The sphere the figure holds contains a real, microscopic crystal — visible only under magnification. When the statuette is held near a mirror, the figure's reflection shows it facing a different direction than the physical object. The inscription on the base, in Draconic, reads: 'FIRST OF THE GRAFT. LAST OF THE LINE.'

interactionStyle.footerText: The reflection lies. The statue remembers.

items.name: Web-Woven Scale Armor
items.shortDescription: Scale armor twisted by the grove's ambient magic. Spider silk threads run between every scale.
items.fullDescription: A suit of medium armor composed of overlapping metallic scales connected by incredibly strong spider silk threads. The scales shift between dark green and deep purple depending on the light, and the silk threads hum faintly when danger is near.
items.interactionPrompt: Run your fingers along the silk threads...
items.hiddenContent: The silk threads vibrate at different frequencies depending on the type of threat nearby: a low hum for physical danger, a high whine for magical threats, and complete silence (ominously) for extraplanar entities. One scale near the collar bears a maker's mark — the symbol of a long-extinct dwarven smithing clan.

interactionStyle.footerText: Silence means something worse than danger.
